title: 3, 3'- diindolylmethane hinders IL-17A/IL-17RA interaction and mitigates imiquimod-induced psoriasiform in mice.
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物化合物DIM抑制IL-17A/IL-17RA蛋白-蛋白相互作用以缓解银屑病，对象为细胞因子受体互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Psoriasis is a highly inflammatory autoimmune-mediated skin disease. The strongest evidence has pointed to the influential role of interleukin (IL) -17A in the aberrant pathology of psoriasis. Henceforth, targeting the IL-17A cytokine is of prime importance in controlling the disease severity of psoriasis. Reportedly, 3, 3'- diindolylmethane (DIM) is a phytochemical that alleviated acute atopic dermatitis. Howbeit, the therapeutic intervention of DIM against IL-17A/IL-17RA interaction and its signaling mediated pathogenesis in psoriasis remains unexplored. In the current report, we decoded the molecular basis of DIM in psoriasis. Docking analysis has reported that DIM identified an IL-17A binding region in the functional fibronectin-III-like domain of IL-17RA and abrogated IL-17A/IL-17RA interaction. In-vitro experiments demonstrated that DIM impeded IL-17A mediated hyper-proliferative phenotype of psoriatic-like keratinocytes. Furthermore, DIM abated the catabolic effects of IL-17A stimulated expression of pathogenic mediators like HMGB-1, Cyr-61, CCL-20, and VEGF via blunted activation of JAK/STAT pathway in psoriatic like keratinocytes. Profoundly, DIM restricted the reprogramming of psoriatic-like keratinocytes to overexpress IL-17RA in concert with IL-17A stimulation. In line with in-vitro studies, DIM also ameliorated skin lesions and epidermal hyperplasia in an imiquimod-induced mice model of psoriasis. Additionally, DIM also reduced STAT-3 phosphorylation and associated expression of Cyr-61, CCL-20, and VEGF in psoriatic mice. However, if DIM has a direct effect on STAT-3 inhibition or it negatively regulates STAT-3 function via blockade of IL-17A/IL-17RA interaction needs to be investigated in the future. Conclusively, our studies demonstrated that the blockade of IL-17A/IL-17RA interaction is a novel therapeutic perspective of DIM against the progression of psoriasis disease.
abstract_zh: 银屑病是一种高度炎症性的自身免疫介导的皮肤病。最有力的证据表明，白细胞介素（IL）-17A在银屑病的异常病理中发挥着关键作用。因此，靶向IL-17A细胞因子对于控制银屑病疾病严重程度至关重要。据报道，3,3'-二吲哚甲烷（DIM）是一种植物化学物质，可缓解急性特应性皮炎。然而，DIM针对IL-17A/IL-17RA相互作用及其信号介导的银屑病发病机制的治疗干预尚未被探索。在本报告中，我们解析了DIM在银屑病中的分子基础。对接分析表明，DIM识别了IL-17RA功能性纤连蛋白-III样结构域中的IL-17A结合区域，并阻断了IL-17A/IL-17RA相互作用。体外实验证明，DIM抑制了IL-17A介导的银屑病样角质形成细胞的过度增殖表型。此外，DIM通过减弱JAK/STAT通路的激活，减轻了IL-17A刺激下致病介质（如HMGB-1、Cyr-61、CCL-20和VEGF）的表达的分解代谢效应。显著地，DIM限制了银屑病样角质形成细胞在IL-17A刺激下过度表达IL-17RA的重编程。与体外研究一致，DIM在咪喹莫特诱导的银屑病小鼠模型中也改善了皮肤病变和表皮增生。此外，DIM还降低了银屑病小鼠中STAT-3磷酸化及Cyr-61、CCL-20和VEGF的相关表达。然而，DIM是否对STAT-3抑制有直接作用，或通过阻断IL-17A/IL-17RA相互作用负向调节STAT-3功能，仍需未来研究。总之，我们的研究表明，阻断IL-17A/IL-17RA相互作用是DIM对抗银屑病疾病进展的新治疗视角。
